expected.name: Taft Holmes
expected.description: Taft Holmes was a Black sharecropper and member of the Share Croppers’ Union near Camp Hill, Alabama. He joined the union after reading its literature and took part in the meetings that preceded the July 1931 confrontation with the sheriff. After union member Ralph Gray was shot and killed, authorities arrested sharecroppers across the area. Holmes was put in jail on Friday evening, July 17. The International Labor Defense campaigned for the arrested workers, and Holmes was later released.

operations.research_note: Original October1931 Labor Defender printed page188 (PDFpage6), Jane Dillon interview, explicitly identifies Taft Holmes of CampHill as age22. Added user-authorized circa1909 birth year; actual year could be1908or1909 depending on birthday. January1 is a storage placeholder, not actual birthday. Article confirms release before interview but supplies no release day/month. Photographs do not identify Holmes; no portrait assigned.
